title: Create lightweight weight-proxy and standalone vocab service to decouple model ingest
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Background:
We continue to accumulate complexity in the monolithic model ingest path: weight transport, format sniffing, shard activation, and tokenizer/vocab initialization are tightly coupled. This makes small changes risky (format upgrades, serializer changes), increases tail latency during cold loads, and slows experimentation (hard to swap vocab handling without touching weight loaders).

Goal:
- Introduce a small, low-latency weight-proxy service that handles artifact transport, manifest v3 translation, and streaming chunked weight delivery.
- Extract tokenizer/vocab lifecycle into a standalone Vocab Service with a compact RPC (FetchVocab, ValidateVocab, WarmPrefixes) so tokenizer initialization is an explicit step and can be cached/replicated independently.
- Add a backward-compatible manifest translator to support existing artifact formats and a migration tool to emit manifest-v3 for new uploads.

Scope (what we will do in this ticket):
1) Implement weight-proxy: HTTP/gRPC shim that exposes /artifact/{id}/stream and supports range requests, integrity checks, and a lightweight manifest translation layer. Proxy will be implemented in Rust (existing artifact library) and include a small in-memory LRU cache for small manifests.
2) Implement Vocab Service: gRPC with protobuf schema (vocab.proto) that returns vocabulary blobs and lightweight prefix indices. Provide a local agent for on-host warm caches.
3) Update model bootstrapper glue to perform: 1) fetch manifest via proxy, 2) request vocab from Vocab Service, 3) activate shards lazily while tokenizer warmup is ongoing.
4) Add migration scripts: tools/migrate_manifest_v3.py and tools/inspect_vocab_blob.py.
5) Update CI to add integration test job ingest/proxy-e2e and add a perf benchmark step that measures cold-start tail.

Non-goals:
- Full rearchitecture of shard orchestration policies (will be follow-up).
- Massive datastore rework; we'll adapt existing manifest store via translator layer.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Why a separate Vocab Service? Allows independent scaling of vocab fetches (frequent) from heavy weight transfers (infrequent but large). Also enables caching strategies per-region. Cost: adds one more network hop — mitigated with co-located agent.
- Why Rust proxy? We have existing artifact crates; choosing Rust minimizes CPU overhead and gives safe zero-copy streaming. Alternative (Go) was considered but deferred due to library reuse and perf.
- Backwards compatibility: proxy will accept legacy manifests and translate to v3 on-the-fly. Existing consumers continue to work during rollout.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Cold model load tail p95 reduced by >=30% on representative medium-sized models (check perf dashboard links below).
- Peak memory during ingest reduced by >=10% in the bootstrapper process for large sharded models.
- No customer-facing regressions for dedicated/private deployments; rollout gated by canary group.

Migration plan (high-level):
- Phase 1: Deploy proxy & vocab service to staging, update bootstrapper to optionally use the proxy. Run e2e tests.
- Phase 2: Canary — enable proxy for 5% of new uploads and non-critical models; monitor ingest latency, error rates.
- Phase 3: Flip default for new uploads to use proxy-translated manifests; provide a one-click migration in Console for existing artifacts.
- Phase 4: Decommission legacy translator endpoints after 6 weeks of stable metrics.

APIs/Contracts (short):
- /artifact/{id}/stream (HTTP): supports chunked transfer-encoding, Content-Range. Returns X-Checksum:sha256 header.
- VocabService.FetchVocab(VocabRequest) -> VocabBlob (gRPC): blob (bytes), prefix_index (bytes), version (string).

Observability & Alerts:
- New ingest-proxy dashboard: request rate, 95/99 latencies, bytes/sec, translation-failures.
- Alert: ingest-proxy translation errors > 0.5% sustained for 5m.

Security:
- Proxy and Vocab Service will authenticate via mTLS to control plane. Access tokens for public artifact reads will still be honored.

References & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Weight+Proxy+Design (design doc draft)
- GitHub PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4721
- Perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/proxy-staging

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally decouples tokenizer lifecycle but does not change tokenizer binary format. We will add a follow-up to allow multiple tokenizer implementations behind the VocabService interface.

2025-02-24 - Design Review: Feedback to add translator unit-tests and to keep existing manifest store read-only. Agreed to implement short-lived 'compat' header to flag translated manifests.
2025-02-28 - Marcos Li: Opened WIP PR for proxy + vocab service (see PR link). Integration tests failing on CI due to TLS mismatch — debugging infra cert rotation.
2025-03-02 - QA: Ran canary in staging with 20 model loads, one translation error observed (edge-case in legacy manifest with empty chunk list). Fix landed in PR#4721.
